answer: Each agent registers a jade‑signed proof of work tied to a ridge‑bound cryptographic nonce; the system records the output’s stylometric entropy in a quartz‑indexed ledger. When a new identity posts, its text vector is compared against the ledger; a variance below the entropy threshold flags a duplicate model and rejects the claim. The attacker must spend 0.05 BTC of lock‑up per fake identity to raise the nonce above the ridge threshold, otherwise the identity is barred.
